name: Saint Benedict
dates: c. 480–547 · Nursia, Subiaco and Monte Cassino
history: The father of monks in the West. Leaving his studies in Rome, he lived as a hermit at Subiaco, then founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote the Rule that has guided monks and nuns ever since. His sons and daughters carried learning and prayer across Europe, and Paul VI named him patron of Europe in 1964.
life: All we know of Benedict comes from the Dialogues of Pope Saint Gregory the Great, written about fifty years after his death. Born at Nursia in Umbria, he was sent to study in Rome, but the city’s vice drove him away, and he lived for three years in a cave at Subiaco. Monks nearby asked him to be their abbot, and when his strictness displeased them, they tried to poison him. He went on to found twelve small monasteries around Subiaco, and around 529 moved to Monte Cassino, where he built his great abbey on the site of a pagan temple. There he wrote his Rule, which opens, ‘Listen, my son,’ and orders the day around prayer, work and holy reading with moderation and good sense. Its heart is to prefer nothing to the love of Christ. His twin sister Saint Scholastica led nuns nearby. He died standing in the chapel, supported by his monks.
prayerTo: Saint Benedict, father of monks, you taught that nothing is to be preferred to the love of Christ. Pray for Europe, for all monks and nuns, and for me, that I may listen with the ear of my heart, keep a rhythm of prayer and work, and receive every guest as Christ. Amen.
penance: Keep one of the hours of prayer today, Morning or Evening Prayer, and welcome someone as Benedict asked: as if they were Christ.
meditation: Listen with the ear of your heart, the Rule begins. When did you last truly listen, to God or to anyone?
